title: Localized pure-tensor extensionality for Hom out of a total tensor
statement: Let (C,J) be a site, R a sheaf of commutative rings, K,L cochain complexes of R-module sheaves, X,N R-module sheaves, and p an integer. Put T=Tot(K tensor L), using [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For a,b : X -> internal Hom(T^p,N), suppose the following holds. For every U, source section s in X(U), W -> U, integers i,j with i+j=p, and sections x in K^i(W), y in L^j(W), the localized maps a_U(s) and b_U(s) have equal values on the image in T^p(W) of x tensor y under the presheaf-to-sheaf tensor comparison and the (i,j) coproduct inclusion. Then a=b. Internal Hom and the presheaf-to-sheaf tensor comparison are those in [lem-sc-hom-tensor-degreewise] and [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. No chosen currying maps or complex morphisms are involved.

proof.text: Fix U and s. Their images are morphisms of module presheaves on the localized site Over U. Restrict these morphisms to every (i,j) total tensor summand with i+j=p. Pure-tensor equality and the bilinear universal property give equality on each presheaf tensor. Sheafification commutes with localization to Over U, so its adjunction extends this equality to each sheaf tensor summand. This uses the canonical comparison homTensorSectionMap, not a claim that sheaf tensor sections are globally sums of pure tensors.

Restriction to Over U preserves coproducts. Thus the coproduct universal property for T^p gives equality of the two localized morphisms. Extensionality in W, s and U gives equality of internal-Hom sections and then of the original sheaf-module morphisms a,b.
